title: The world's longest known cave runs for more than 686 km under Kentucky
body: Mammoth Cave began forming about **330 million years ago** in thick layers of limestone. Groundwater seeping through the rock slowly dissolved it, hollowing out passages at different levels over millions of years. A cap of sandstone on top keeps the system remarkably stable. By 2025, cavers had surveyed more than 686 km of passages, over 1.5 times the length of the second-longest known cave system, Ox Bel Ha in Mexico, and new discoveries still add more every year.

cover.alt: A tall metal staircase climbing up inside Mammoth Dome, a towering shaft in the cave lit orange against fluted limestone walls

slides.heading: How a limestone cave is carved

steps.label: Passages open up level by level

slides.prompt: In 1972 cavers found a link between Mammoth Cave and something else. What?
slides.answer: An even longer cave system under Flint Ridge
slides.detail: The final connection was made on 9 September 1972. Since then the combined network has been known as the Mammoth–Flint Ridge Cave System.

events.text: Wartime miners dig saltpetre for gunpowder
Enslaved guide Stephen Bishop maps and names many passages

slides.question: Why did miners dig in Mammoth Cave during the War of 1812?
options: For gold in the cave streams
slides.explanation: A trade embargo cut off imports, starving the American military of saltpetre and so of gunpowder. Mining the cave for nitrates suddenly paid.
